claims.statement: Extending an original leaf by one pendant edge can change the fixed-rank favorable tagged family and its complete aggregate even when the same rank remains eligible before and after the operation.
claims.scope: One exact eligible pair at p=8, together with exact polynomial, selector, support, and summand recurrences for pendant extension at a leaf; this is not a refutation of the primary aggregate inequality.
claims.reason: In the encoded 18- and 19-vertex trees, both rows have x=6 and alpha=12 and satisfy both primary guards. The extension removes old leaf tag 10, adds favorable leaf tag 18, changes support multiplicities, and changes the complete sums from -4256 to -6267. The recurrences give exact conditional checks but no universal sign theorem or valid minimal-counterexample reduction.

limitations: The exact calculation is one pair of trees and is not exhaustive.
No positive complete-sum counterexample or universal proof was obtained.
A useful extension-based reduction still needs explicit hypotheses controlling the new first descent, all surviving and new selector signs, both guards, and the full transformed aggregate.
